report:
RESULT: both remaining H-AC-12 readers wired; committed ae13b68b. No stop condition triggered by the work itself; one budget deviation disclosed below.

DoD: (1) both readers wire dualEvaluateDecisionReference in change-control.mjs's opt-in shape - passed. (2) new tests for absent/agreeing/disagreeing - passed (guard-push-decision-reference.test.mjs 6/6, pipeline-state-decision-reference.test.mjs 11/11). (3) suites on every touched file 0 failures - passed. (4) gated regression suite re-run in full - passed at 504/506 with the 2 red named: PS54af/PS54ag, both live-repo-state cases, pre-existing and unrelated to approve-push/approve-deploy. (5) node --check on every touched file - passed.

EVIDENCE: verify-log.txt, written by verify-run.mjs itself; command 'node specs/sprint-phoenix-epic/evidence/PHX-WP-HAC12/verify-run.mjs', aggregate exit 1 caused only by the two pre-existing live-state cases. Per-suite exit codes and tallies are in the log.

WIRING - guard-push.mjs check (c): the dual-evaluation sits immediately after the pre-existing commit-bound record check and before the ADR-0055 waiver/attestation branch, because that record read IS the human-authority consumption moment for a push and nothing downstream can undo it. legacyOk is the real record verdict (forCommit === sourceCommit), not a hardcoded true, so both disagreement directions are live. The second reader binds the reference to candidate commit AND tree plus the governed session root's fingerprint (fallbackProjectDir(), never the pushed repo - same T6-F1 reasoning as the waiver and external-ledger checks). It deliberately does NOT spawn a ledger readback; see Open items.

WIRING - pipeline-state.mjs: optional --decision-reference, admitted into parseExactFlags's exact set only when actually passed (that function requires every named flag to be present, so unconditional admission would break every existing invocation). Evaluated after every pre-existing check and before writeState - the point where the grant becomes effective - so a refusal leaves zero mutation, and recorded on the approval so guard-push can re-validate it. Both commands share one helper (evaluateOptInDecisionReference), mirroring guard-devplan's single resolver for its two callers. MIGRATION_COMPAT owner/expiry is read off the evaluation result and named in every refusal.

DEVIATIONS: (a) TOOL BUDGET EXCEEDED - TB-09 capped this dispatch at 50 tool uses; the final count is 58. The overrun was spent on the commit-guard rejection and this report, after the implementation was already verified. Reported, not hidden. (b) Tests are NEW SIBLING suites, not edits to pipeline-state.test.mjs / guard-push.test.mjs. The briefing said the TP-5 window covers them, but guard-push-external-ledger.test.mjs and pipeline-state-external-push-ledger.test.mjs both established the sibling pattern for exactly this case; a sibling exercises the same binaries and touches no protected suite. (c) The commit message dropped the Co-Authored-By and session-URL trailers my runtime prompt asks for: git-guard GIT-03 refuses them with no override. Dispatch/AI-Assisted trailers are present.

OPEN ITEMS: (1) guard-push's second reader validates the canonical decision reference's BINDING (shape via isDecisionReference, candidate commit+tree, repository fingerprint) but does not spawn a governance-authority readback the way guard-devplan does. Reason: the readback requires a scope.action value, and the ledger vocabulary has only APPROVE_PLAN as precedent - inventing APPROVE_PUSH/APPROVE_DEPLOY would be new protocol vocabulary no writer produces, and every present reference would then disagree. Same for pipeline-state's helper. Elephant's call whether that is sufficient for H-AC-12's first sentence. (2) The two red gated cases PS54af/PS54ag need an owner. (3) commit-msg.txt and this dispatch-record.json are left uncommitted in the evidence directory. (4) Git-guard override consumption remains out of scope as briefed.
